data.name: WhatEachServiceChargesNote
data.value: What each service charges. Cost is worked out from these at the moment you look, never stored with the usage — published prices change, and a figure baked into a release six months ago is a number that looks authoritative and is wrong. The values below are the list prices at the time this version was built; correct any that have moved. Rates are entered at the scale each vendor quotes them in, shown beside every row. A provider with no row here is counted as unpriced, not as free — only the rows marked local are genuinely free.

data.name: EachAlarmIsCheckedNote
data.value: Each alarm is checked on its own interval, so the loop only touches the database when one is actually due. An alarm announces only what it has not announced before — a condition that stays true does not repeat itself — which is why a check that keeps matching shows here as armed rather than as firing over and over.

data.name: EveryThirtySecondsAndNote
data.value: Every thirty seconds, and at once after a poll brings in jobs, contracts or assets, each pending order in the Order Tracker is matched against what could fill it: a contract issued by one of your characters or personal corporations to that buyer after the order was placed completes it outright; otherwise unreserved stock on hand, or the soonest industry job producing the item, whose completion date becomes the order's estimated date. Stock and jobs are reserved as they are claimed, so two orders never count the same units, and a contract already linked to one order is never reused for another.
data.comment: Note in BackgroundProcessesView.

data.name: CollectsPlayerStructureIdsNote
data.value: Collects player-structure IDs from assets, contracts, industry jobs, market orders and wallet entries, then resolves each one's name, type, owner and position. Sweeps hourly; the public structure list is walked once a day for structures nobody here has visited. Rows our own assets identify as ships, containers or asset-safety wraps are removed rather than kept as unknown structures. Resolving needs esi-universe.read_structures.v1 and docking access, so a private structure stays unresolved — those are the ones worth describing by hand in the Structure Browser.
data.comment: Note in BackgroundProcessesView.
